speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me how long you have been experiencing this abdominal pain and weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant amount of weight to lose in such a short time, especially combined with night sweats. Can you describe the location of the abdominal pain and whether you have noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: A painless, fixed, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph node is a concerning sign that often points toward malignancy, particularly given your other symptoms. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Cervical Lymph Node Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Blood Work: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal, Lactate Dehydrogenase Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, combined with your B-symptoms and enlarged lymph nodes, strongly indicates a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
